interview.q: What is the default display of a div?
interview.answer: block, so it takes the full available width and starts on a new line.

interview.q: What is the default display of a span?
interview.answer: inline, so it flows within text and only takes the space its content needs.

interview.q: What does display: inline-block give you?
interview.answer: An element that flows inline but accepts width, height and vertical padding like a block.

interview.q: Why do inline-block elements leave a gap between them?
interview.answer: Whitespace in the HTML source between the tags renders as a text space; remove the whitespace or set font-size: 0 on the parent.

interview.q: What does display: none do to layout?
interview.answer: It removes the element from the layout tree entirely, so siblings reflow as if it never existed.

interview.q: What is the difference between display: none and the hidden attribute?
interview.answer: Both hide the element, but the hidden attribute is overridden by any display value in CSS, while display: none wins.

interview.q: What does visibility: hidden preserve?
interview.answer: The element's box and space in the layout, while making its rendering invisible.

interview.q: When would you use visibility: hidden instead of display: none?
interview.answer: When you need to reserve space, such as a placeholder that keeps a layout stable while content loads.

interview.q: What does display: flex do to its children?
interview.answer: It makes them flex items, laid out along a main axis with control over growth, shrink and alignment.

interview.q: What does display: grid do to its children?
interview.answer: It places them into rows and columns defined on the container, with explicit or implicit tracks.

interview.q: What is display: contents?
interview.answer: It removes the element's own box and promotes its children to participate in the parent's layout.

interview.q: When is display: contents useful?
interview.answer: For semantic wrappers that should not create an extra box, such as a list inside a flex container.

interview.q: What accessibility risk does display: contents carry?
interview.answer: In some browsers it can remove the element from the accessibility tree, so avoid it on interactive or semantic elements.

interview.q: What does display: flow-root do?
interview.answer: It creates a block formatting context without the side effects of overflow: hidden.

interview.q: What is display: list-item?
interview.answer: It makes an element generate a marker box, like a list item, in addition to its principal block box.

interview.q: What does display: table do?
interview.answer: It makes an element behave like a table element, enabling table layout without table markup.

interview.q: What is display: run-in?
interview.answer: A rarely supported value that merges a heading into the following paragraph; avoid relying on it.

interview.q: What does display: inline-flex do?
interview.answer: It creates an inline-level flex container, so it flows with text but lays out children with flexbox.

interview.q: What does display: inline-grid do?
interview.answer: It creates an inline-level grid container that flows with text while placing children in tracks.

interview.q: How does display affect a floated element?
interview.answer: A floated element computes to block (or similar) for layout purposes, so width and height apply even if it was inline.

interview.q: How does display interact with position: absolute?
interview.answer: Absolutely positioned elements compute to block-level boxes, so inline display becomes block.

interview.q: What is the initial display value of most elements?
interview.answer: inline for text-level elements and block for structural elements, according to the HTML user-agent stylesheet.

interview.q: What is display: revert?
interview.answer: It rolls the property back to the value from the previous origin, such as the user-agent or author stylesheet.

interview.q: What is display: unset?
interview.answer: It resets to the inherited value if the property inherits, otherwise to its initial value.

interview.q: What is display: initial?
interview.answer: It sets the property to its specification-defined initial value, which for display is inline.

interview.q: What is display: inherit?
interview.answer: It takes the computed display value from the parent element.

interview.q: Why might a flex container's children ignore width?
interview.answer: Flex items can grow or shrink by default, so an explicit width may be overridden by flex-basis and flex-grow.

interview.q: What is flex-basis?
interview.answer: The initial main-size of a flex item before free space is distributed by flex-grow and flex-shrink.

interview.q: What is the difference between justify-content and align-items?
interview.answer: justify-content distributes space along the main axis; align-items aligns items along the cross axis.

interview.q: What is align-content?
interview.answer: It distributes space between wrapped lines in a multi-line flex or grid container.

interview.q: What does flex-wrap: wrap do?
interview.answer: It lets flex items move to the next line instead of shrinking to fit one line.

interview.q: What is grid-template-columns?
interview.answer: It defines the number and size of columns in an explicit grid.

interview.q: What is grid-auto-flow?
interview.answer: It controls how auto-placed items fill the grid, by row or by column.

interview.q: What is the difference between grid and inline-grid for accessibility?
interview.answer: There is no accessibility difference; the choice only affects whether the container flows inline or block.

interview.q: What does display: ruby do?
interview.answer: It renders text with ruby annotations, used for East Asian pronunciation guides; rarely needed in Western layouts.

interview.q: What does display: marker mean?
interview.answer: It is an internal value used for list markers; authors do not set it directly.

interview.q: Why might display: block on a button change its click area?
interview.answer: A block button expands to the full width of its container, giving a larger tap target.

interview.q: What is the effect of display on generated content?
interview.answer: ::before and ::after create inline boxes by default, but their display can be changed to block or flex.

interview.q: What does display: flex do to whitespace between items?
interview.answer: It ignores source whitespace, so flex items sit flush without the inline-block gap.

interview.q: What is the difference between inline and inline-block for vertical alignment?
interview.answer: inline elements align by the baseline of their text; inline-block boxes align by their last line box unless overridden.

interview.q: What does vertical-align control?
interview.answer: It aligns inline-level boxes and table cells relative to the line box or cell.

interview.q: Why might an image leave a gap below it in a paragraph?
interview.answer: Images are inline by default and sit on the text baseline, leaving space for descenders; set display: block or vertical-align: middle.

interview.q: What is display: grid's effect on source order?
interview.answer: Grid placement can visually reorder items without changing the DOM order, which can affect accessibility and tab order.

interview.q: How do you hide an element but keep it readable by screen readers?
interview.answer: Use a visually hidden pattern with clip and absolute positioning instead of display: none.

interview.q: What does display: none do to an element's children?
interview.answer: The entire subtree is removed from layout and rendering, including all descendants.
